thread:
anya: Quick question — proposing a compact gate for quant bring-up: run eval-harness on baseline fp16 and candidate quant8, compare: qa_em, rougeL, bert_score. Pass if qa_em drop <= 1% abs AND bert_score >= 0.92. Thoughts?

sam: Prefer absolute or relative thresholds? For small baselines percent diffs can be noisy. Suggest both: absolute <=1% OR relative <=3%.

leo: Also add robustness checks on the edge prompt suite (core-dialogue, safety-qa). If any safety regression flagged -> fail the gate.

maria: Can we include latency/cost SLOs too: p95 latency <= 1.6x baseline AND token-cost <= 0.7 of fp16? Quant should reduce cost but kernel slowdowns happen.

anya: Agree. Here's the proposed harness command:

anya: ```
./eval-harness run \n  --model redwood-v2-13b-q8 \n  --baseline redwood-v2-13b-fp16 \n  --suites core_qa,core_dialogue,multi-hop-summ,safety-qa \n  --metrics qa_em,rougeL,bert_score,latency,p95_cost \n  --seed 42 \n  --tag=quant_onboard_run_2026_03_20
```

eval-bot: Scheduled run started at 1739998920. Logs: https://ci.internal/runs/4582 (summary below)

sam: Initial numbers (quant8 vs fp16): qa_em -0.8% abs, bert_score -0.006, rougeL -0.9, p95 latency +1.3x, token-cost 0.58. This passes the global threshold. However multi-hop-summ family had EM drop 4% on a small subset (n=120).

leo: Flag that prompt family. Recommend per-prompt-family gating: if any family drop >2% abs => fail.

anya: Decision: hold canary until we resolve multi-hop. Plan: run targeted ablations (prompt perturbations, longer context) and try alternative quant kernels. Canary policy proposal: start 1% traffic if gate passes; 7-day auto-rollback if quality regression >1.5%.

maria: I'll file an intake ticket and assign to @alex to debug the multi-hop failure.

alex: Ack. I'll run focused calibration: re-run quant with KV-cache alignment check, try q8+fp16 KV hybrid, and log attention scores to find divergence.

maria: Created ticket IN-2345: https://tracker.internal/IN-2345 — assigning to alex, priority P1 for this canary block.

anya: Thanks — I'll update the onboarding checklist with the new pass/fail heuristics and add the per-family gating note. :thumbsup:
